literal_meaning: ঢাকের পিঠে বাঁশ (drum's back/surface with bamboo)
similar_in_english: a square peg in a round hole
example_sentences_in_bangla: এই প্রস্তাব তো ঢাকের পিঠে বাঁশ, কোনো কাজে লাগবে না।
তার চেষ্টা ঢাকের পিঠে বাঁশের মতো ব্যর্থ হবে।
example_sentences_in_english: This proposal is like bamboo on a drum's back; it won't work at all.
His effort will be futile, just like putting bamboo on a drum.
history: The idiom originates from the traditional Bengali drum (dhak), which is played with sticks, not bamboo, highlighting the absurdity of an ill-suited or impossible action.
note: Refers to the cultural use of dhak in festivals and rural music.
